intended_object: The degree-two relation space R ⊆ kQ₂ of the quadratic presentation of the Huerfano–Khovanov zigzag algebra of a simple graph G. It is the k-span, inside the path algebra of the doubled quiver, of the length-two paths i→j→l with i ≠ l and of the differences (i→j→i) − (i→j'→i) of backtracks at the same vertex. This is inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and the Huerfano–Khovanov reference.
explanation:
The definition is the k-submodule spanned by `IsQuadraticZigzagRelator k G`. That predicate has two constructors:
- `nonreturn`: a length-two path whose endpoints differ;
- `equal_backtracks`: the difference of two length-two loops at the same vertex.

In the doubled quiver, i → j has exactly one arrow when G.Adj i j and none otherwise. A simple graph has no loops, so every length-two path from i back to i is a backtrack i→j→i. The two families are therefore exactly the quadratic zigzag relations of Huerfano–Khovanov: (i|j|l) = 0 for i ≠ l, and (i|j|i) = (i|j'|i).

The docstring says the space lies "inside the degree-two part". The definition itself is a submodule of the whole path algebra, but the very next lemma, `quadraticZigzagRelations_le_grade_two`, proves that it lies in degree two. This is the standard way to set up the relation space before taking its quadratic dual.

The length-three relations are left out on purpose. The module explains that they are redundant for connected graphs with at least three vertices, and that this is where the presentation applies.

Requiring `CommRing k` is the usual base-ring setting for path algebras and for quadratic duality, so it is not too narrow. Mathlib has no zigzag algebra or quadratic zigzag relations.
